elements.text: Flight crew's failure to maintain adequate airspeed after shutting down the right engine due to in-flight fire
Failure to maintain airspeed resulting in aerodynamic stall or loss of directional control
Flight crew likely did not use ADI and autofeather systems during takeoff
Accident airplane exceeded maximum allowable takeoff weight due to nonuse of ADI and autofeather
Flight crew feathered left propeller late in the accident sequence
At least one engine generating thrust until near the end of the flight
Airspeed reduced to point of aerodynamic stall or below minimum control speed during right turn
Ignition of flammable liquid in one of the right augmentors
Leak in vicinity of augmentor/muffler junction allowing fire to exit and damage right wing
First officer's limited recent experience and performance deficiencies in training/certification
Captain suffering from acute sleep loss affecting ability to guide first officer
Fresh Air failed to keep accurate and complete records
FAA did not address Fresh Air’s deficient recordkeeping
FAA’s oversight of Fresh Air’s recordkeeping was inadequate
FAA inspectors failed to perform effective oversight of Fresh Air
Belief that Part 125 operations merit less scrutiny than Part 121 and 135 operations
Principal operations inspector unaware airplanes were operated contrary to approved flight manual limitations
FAA failed to ensure captain was evaluated on OpsSpecs knowledge within 12 months before accident
FAA inspector guidance did not specify evaluation on OpsSpecs for pilots under Part 125 lateral moves
